summary_en: Vision Inc. withdrew its medium-term management plan and adopted a progressive dividend policy with an annual dividend floor of 51 yen per share. The company will maintain or increase dividends based on earnings performance, replacing previous targets of 50% payout ratio and 8% DOE, while prioritizing growth investments including M&A.
title_en: Notice Regarding Withdrawal of Medium-Term Management Plan and Change in Dividend Policy (Introduction of Progressive Dividend)
translation_en_brief:
Vision Inc. announced a fundamental revision of its capital allocation policy by withdrawing its medium-term management plan and introducing a progressive dividend framework. The company had previously committed to a 50% payout ratio and 8% dividend on equity (DOE) through fiscal 2028, but changed course due to significant external headwinds affecting its core Global WiFi business. The company cited Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions, fuel surcharge volatility, prolonged historical yen weakness, and resulting shifts in consumer travel patterns toward shorter, more budget-conscious trips. Corporate customer acquisition grew, but actual business travel demand fell short of projections amid uncertainty.

Under the new policy, Vision has set an annual dividend floor of 51 yen per share, maintaining this year's forecast unchanged. The company commits to a progressive dividend approach: it will avoid dividend cuts in principle and aim to maintain or increase dividends as earnings improve. This replaces the rigid performance-linked targets that previously constrained strategic flexibility.

The company emphasized that fixed financial targets under high uncertainty could impede agile strategic adjustments and growth investment decisions. By prioritizing growth capital for M&A and strategic investments while combining stable dividend maintenance with opportunistic share buybacks, Vision aims to improve capital efficiency and earnings per share on a total shareholder return basis.
